corrections.text: The summary says kernel docs "already require Assisted-by tags." The kernel's AI Coding Assistants page says contributions "should include an Assisted-by tag"; it does not use the word "require" for that tag. The page's mandatory language ("MUST NOT") applies to AI agents adding Signed-off-by tags.

The headline's "First" comes from LWN's own headline, "Linus Torvalds's first LLM-assisted patch series," and refers to Torvalds's own first such series. The article does not establish that this is the first LLM-assisted patch series in the Linux kernel, and the kernel's documentation shows AI-assisted contributions were already anticipated.

The article calls the quoted passage a "series description." LWN presents the passage as an unattributed block quote and does not say it is from the series cover letter. The order-of-magnitude speedup on a read()-heavy benchmark is LWN's statement of the result, not a quoted claim by Torvalds.
